title: CFD: checkpoint and resume complete CPU fluid state
body:
## What and why

Refs #653. A stopped CPU fluid solve can continue from an explicit restart file rather than repeat the run. The checkpoint retains population buffers, outlet/fan and conducting-solid state, output cursors and histories, partial steady windows, LES eddy-viscosity state, and complete running-average accumulators.

Resume restores the same result, statistics and stopping decision bit for bit. Model, geometry, physical settings and caps must match; CPU thread count and storage cadence may change. `checkpoint_every` is required whenever a checkpoint path is supplied, including resume, so a large solve never silently rewrites its complete state every 64 steps.

The streamed, versioned format bounds memory, validates shapes and finite values, checks identity and SHA-256, and atomically replaces only a recognized checkpoint. Cancellation preserves the latest sound save. The solver-state layout is now `FCRST2`; it is not a cross-version migration format. Display results in a project remain separate from restart state.

Three logical commits cover solver state, native persistence, and commands/forms/docs.

## Validation

Tested revision: `afef7b10972d195953d69fa0dad5cfcab5b32e18`, rebased onto `3751d3bb93676aa49d1a18c438424be88162ac03`. Current verification is Linux CPU-only.

- `cargo check` and normal suites: LBM 84 passed (22 existing ignores), engine 379 passed (15 existing ignores), IO 76 passed (1 existing ignore); no baseline failures.
- All 10 checkpoint regressions pass, including heated LES with averaging before/after the interruption, both collisions, early steady stopping, changed cadence and changed CPU thread count. Complete results and retained floating-point state match bit for bit.
- Scoped all-target clippy with `-D warnings`, formatting and diff checks pass.
- The identical `fieldcraft_engine::catalogue::features_page()` generator was invoked through a temporary Rust wrapper against the tested engine; output exactly matches `docs/features.md`.
- GPU execution, the full workspace gate, heavy suites and oracle were not run. The numerical scheme and numerical fixtures are unchanged.

## Historical demonstration

These attachments retain their original capture revision. They demonstrate the earlier restart workflow, before the new LES/averaging state and thread-independent identity changes; they are not a new UI verification of this revision.

<!-- fieldcraft-attachments:start -->
### Attached files

These uploads are complete; earlier pending-upload wording below describes the original handoff.

Capture/source revision: `c3867d6cd1647171a01a84cb30c5d68af30f2fb8`.

**cpu-checkpoint-653.mp4**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfd45ff2-1691-4d62-b4ba-6c3ed7064c9c

**cpu-restart-flow.png**

![cpu-restart-flow.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ae0e3ce-cbc4-4211-be31-489ec2f1d476)

**cpu-restart-form.png**

The original clip uses a 64-cell CPU flow and shows cancellation, retained state, changed save cadence and completion. The RTX 4090 rendered its viewport; the solver was CPU. It is edited frame playback rather than a real-time recording. No media belongs to feature history.

## Limits

GPU, other solvers, browser restart, automatic discovery and wall-clock scheduling remain open under #653. Each save rewrites retained state and may be large; atomic replacement temporarily needs space for old and new files. Concurrent writers need separate paths. A hard kill can leave an unpublished adjacent temporary file. This checks continuation fidelity, not additional physical accuracy.

reviews.author: jyviko
reviews.body:
Thank you, this is careful work! The atomic writes, size caps, the identity refusal and the bit-for-bit resume tests are all excellent. #711 (LES and running averages) landed since, so a few things need to follow:

1. **Rebase.** It conflicts in `crates/engine/src/cmd/solve.rs`.
2. **Save #711's state.** `Monitor::checkpoint` (`steady.rs:175`) doesn't save the running averages (`sum`, `squares`, `least`, `most`, `count`), and `Flow::checkpoint` doesn't save `cell_nu_t` or `eddy_ratio`. A resumed averaged or Smagorinsky run would give wrong averages and stop decisions, and nothing flags it because those files merge cleanly. Please save them and add resume-parity tests with turbulence and averaging on.
3. **Default `checkpoint_every` = 64** (`solve.rs:818`) rewrites all populations plus every frame, then fsyncs and hashes the file. On a real grid that dominates the run. Please make it explicit, or default to a fraction of the run (e.g. steps/20).
4. **Drop the thread count from the identity** (`solve.rs:851`). CPU results are bit-identical on any thread count, so it only blocks resuming on another machine.

Nit: the unstable-step rewind (`lbm/src/solve.rs:425`) re-derives the event schedule by hand, so it would break quietly when a new event type is added.
